history.summary: filteredHist()의 거래 내역 검색(가계부의 '메모·카테고리·자산 검색')이 메모/카테고리/보내는-받는 자산명을 대소문자 구분 없이 매칭해야 하는데 순수 String.includes(q)로 대소문자를 그대로 비교하고 있어, 영문 메모나 자산명(예: 'Coffee Shop', 'KakaoBank')을 소문자로 검색하면 못 찾는 실제 버그였다(index.html filteredHist, 3050번대). 검색 매칭 로직을 순수 함수 matchTxnQuery(t,q,assets)로 추출해 hay.toLowerCase().includes(q.toLowerCase())로 바꿨다 — 삭제된 자산의 경우 기존엔 fa가 없으면 assetNm(id,snap)을 다시 호출해 DB.assets를 한 번 더(못 찾을 걸 알면서) 훑고 snap으로 폴백했는데, 새 함수는 assets 파라미터로 전달된 배열에서만 찾고 못 찾으면 바로 t.fromAssetName/toAssetName 스냅샷으로 폴백해 동일한 결과를 내면서도 전역 DB에 의존하지 않아 테스트 가능해졌다(동작 변화 없음, 순수화만). filteredHist는 이제 이 함수를 호출하도록 교체. test/run.js에 matchTxnQuery를 추출 대상으로 추가하고 회귀 테스트 5개 추가(빈 검색어, 대문자 메모를 소문자로 검색, 대문자로 검색해 소문자 자산명 찾기, 삭제된 자산의 스냅샷 이름 매칭, 매칭 없음) — 81/81 통과(기존 76개 + 신규 5개). 두 인라인 <script> 블록 모두 new Function()으로 파싱 확인. cycle12 critique 계획대로 recApply()/recSave()의 부분 수정 경로(scope='one'/'future')에 twGuard+undo를 통일했다. 두 함수 맨 앞에 if(twGuard())return;을 추가해 튜토리얼 중 실제 DB 반영을 막았고, recApply의 scope='one' 삭제(r.skip.push)는 push 전 배열 스냅샷을, scope='future' 삭제(r.endDate 절단)는 이전 endDate 스냅샷을 떠서 각각 undoToast로 되돌릴 수 있게 했다(scope='all'은 기존처럼 deleteRecsUndo로 위임, 변경 없음). recSave()의 세 분기도 동일하게: scope='one'은 edits[date] 덮어쓰기 전 이전 값(없었으면 undefined)을 스냅샷해 undo 시 원래 상태로 복원(이전에 없었으면 키 자체를 delete), scope='future'는 endDate 스냅샷 + 새로 push한 분리 레코드를 undo 시 filter로 제거, scope='all'은 r.amount 스냅샷 후 복원. 두 함수 모두 plain toast 대신 undoToast()로 교체했다. test/run.js에 recApply/recSave를 추출 대상에 추가하고(uid/closeSheet/renderTxSheet 스텁, $('txAmt') 값을 반환하는 $ 스텁, window 전역 신설) 9개 회귀 테스트 추가(scope별 적용+undo 3쌍, edits 덮어쓰기 case, 튜토리얼 차단 2건) -- 69/69 통과. 디버깅 중 vm.createContext 샌드박스에서 만들어진 객체/배열은 메인 realm과 프로토타입이 달라 assert.deepStrictEqual이 실패한다는 걸 발견해, 그런 값은 개별 프로퍼티(assert.strictEqual)나 길이 비교로 검증하도록 테스트를 수정했다(기존 배열 비교 테스트들은 애초에 메인 realm에서 만든 배열을 push/filter만 했기 때문에 문제없이 통과했던 것). 두 인라인 <script> 블록 모두 node --check로 파싱 확인. Found a real, scoped accessibility gap: openSheet()'s default close button (index.html ~4120, class .sheet-x) is the icon-only ${svg('x')} button rendered on virtually every modal/sheet in the app whenever no custom topBtn is passed — by far the single most-used interactive control in the whole UI — and it had zero text alternative for screen readers, unlike most named buttons elsewhere. The picker back button (.pk-back, ~4894, used in every openPicker() screen) had the same gap. Accessibility had been flagged as a real but 'diffuse/low-priority' runner-up in critique cycles 6-8 and never acted on because it read as too broad for one cycle; these two are the two highest-reach, lowest-risk instances (each defined exactly once, used everywhere) so fixing just these two closes most of the practical gap without touching any business logic. Added aria-label="닫기" to .sheet-x and aria-label="뒤로" to .pk-back. Pure HTML-attribute change, no JS logic touched, so no new regression tests needed — ran the full existing suite (49/49 pass) and re-verified both inline <script> blocks parse via new Function(). Bumped APP_VERSION 1.19.2→1.19.3 and sw.js CACHE v45→v46 (patch bump, accessibility fix).

Implemented cycle 8's critique plan: added a pure totalBudgetSummary(rows,budgets) that, given spendByCategory() rows and DB.budgets, sums budgetedTotal/spentOnBudgeted across only the categories that have a budget set, counts overCount (categories over their budget) and unsetCount (categories with spending but no budget), and returns budgetedTotal=0 when no budgets exist at all (nothing to aggregate). Verified both inline <script> blocks still parse via new Function(). Bumped APP_VERSION 1.19.1→1.19.2 and sw.js CACHE v44→v45 (patch bump, additive UI feature reusing existing data/helpers).

Implemented cycle 5's critique plan: connected the previously-dead DB.budgets scaffolding to a real feature by extending the existing openSpendAnalysis() ('지출 분석') sheet instead of building a new screen. Tapping a category row now opens openBudgetPrompt(idx), which reads/writes DB.budgets[category] via saveBudget()/delBudget(). Extracted the percentage math into a pure budgetProgress(spent,budget) helper: when a budget is set, the row's progress bar switches from 'share of total spend' to 'usage vs budget' (clamped to 100% width so the bar never overflows), turns from --brand to --expense once spending exceeds the budget, and the amount/percentage text also gets the --expense highlight; categories with no budget keep today's total-share behavior unchanged. doRenameCat() now migrates DB.budgets[old]->DB.budgets[new] on expense-category rename, mirroring the existing catIcon/catVar migration pattern (delCat leaves orphaned budget entries alone, same as it already does for catIcon/catVar). Added 6 new regression tests (budgetProgress edge cases including the 0-budget divide-by-zero guard and the >100% clamp, plus the rename-migrates-budget case) — all 24 tests pass. Bumped APP_VERSION 1.17.3->1.17.4 and sw.js CACHE v38->v39.

delCat(k,i) only spliced the category out of DB.categories[k] but never cleaned up DB.catIcon[catKey(k,c)], DB.catVar[catKey(k,c)], or (for expense) DB.budgets[c] — the exact same class of orphaned-parallel-map bug that doRenameCat already had to fix for rename, but delete was never given the same treatment. Since catKey is purely name-based, deleting a category (e.g. '커피' with a custom icon, a '변동' flag, and a 30,000원 budget) and later re-adding one with the same name silently inherited the old icon/variable-flag/budget the user never set. Extracted the deletion body into doDeleteCat(k,i), mirroring doRenameCat's migration pattern, which now also deletes the catIcon/catVar entries and (for k==='expense') the budgets entry for the deleted category name; delCat() just calls it inside the existing confirmSheet callback. Added 3 new regression tests to test/run.js (icon/var/budget cleanup on delete, no inheritance on same-name re-add, and a guard that non-expense types don't touch DB.budgets) — all 27 tests pass. Verified both inline <script> blocks still parse via `new Function()`. Bumped APP_VERSION 1.17.4→1.17.5 and sw.js CACHE v39→v40.

Reviewed commit 6aba2c4 (doDeleteCat cleanup fix). Verified doDeleteCat mirrors doRenameCat's existing catIcon/catVar/budgets migration pattern correctly (same catKey-based lookups, same expense-only guard for DB.budgets), confirmed migrate() always initializes DB.catIcon/catVar/budgets so the new deletes are never against undefined objects, checked there is no second category-deletion code path that bypasses doDeleteCat (delCat is the only caller of DB.categories[k].splice), re-ran the regression suite (27/27 pass) and re-validated both inline <script> blocks parse via new Function(). No bugs found — no code changes this phase.

Stepped back to look at the whole app rather than the last commit. Found the app has no net-worth history/trend view at all — only ever shows a single 'now' snapshot — and the codebase itself shows this was started and abandoned: orphaned comments at index.html lines 159/167/1912/1914 ('① 현금흐름 곡선 카드', '현금흐름 곡선 그리기 (canvas)') plus a dead .fc-chart canvas CSS rule, with zero implementing function or <canvas> element anywhere (confirmed via grep). Also noted a structural gap that constrains the fix: DB.rates only stores a current price snapshot, no history, so any trend implementation must snapshot already-evaluated totals (via assetEval()/netWorth()) rather than trying to recompute past non-cash asset values from today's rates. Runner-up candidates noted but not chosen: accessibility is essentially absent (5 total aria-/role=/alt=/tabindex hits across 5172 lines), local auth password hashing is an unsalted djb2 hash (low real-world risk, local-only), and there's no CSV/spreadsheet export (JSON backup/restore only). Wrote the net-worth-history plan to pending_advance_plan for the next advance cycle. No code changed this phase.

Implemented cycle 6's critique plan: connected the net-worth history gap by adding DB.nwHistory=DB.nwHistory||[] to migrate() and two pure functions — updateNwHistory(hist,dateStr,ta,td) (append-or-update-today, immutable) and pruneNwHistory(hist) (keeps daily granularity for the most recent 90 days, compresses anything older to one snapshot per month, only kicks in above 120 entries so normal usage never touches it). Wired the snapshot into startApp() (covers first-ever open and every reopen, refreshing today's entry) and into refreshToday()'s day-changed branch (covers the app staying open across midnight) — both call save() right after, matching the existing changed-then-save() convention. Added nwChartPath(pts,W,H), a pure function producing an SVG path string (min/max-normalized, span-zero-safe) with no chart library, and nwHistoryCard() which renders it as an inline <svg> sparkline card (shown only once ≥2 snapshots exist) inserted into renderAssets() right after the net-worth carousel. Replaced the entire dead cash-flow-curve CSS block (.flow-card/.fc-head/.fc-lb/.fc-end/.fc-sub/.fc-chart/.fc-foot/.fc-stat/.fs-k/.fs-v — verified via grep that none of these classes were referenced anywhere outside their own definitions) with real .nwh-card/.nwh-range/.nwh-chart rules, and replaced the orphaned '① 현금흐름 곡선 카드' / '현금흐름 곡선 그리기 (canvas)' comments with the real nwHistoryCard() implementation, putting the previously-unused shortDate2() helper to actual use. Added 8 new regression tests (updateNwHistory append/update-in-place/immutability, pruneNwHistory below-threshold and month-compression behavior, nwChartPath's <2-points/flat-line/rising-line cases) — all 35 tests pass. Verified both inline <script> blocks still parse via new Function(). Bumped APP_VERSION 1.17.5→1.18.0 and sw.js CACHE v40→v41 (minor bump, not patch, since this adds a new schema field and a new UI section rather than fixing a bug).

addCat(k) was the odd one out among the app's 'add/rename named item' flows: addOwner() and doRenameCat() both check for a duplicate name and toast('이미 있는 카테고리예요'/'이미 있는 귀속이에요') before returning, but addCat() just silently skipped the DB.categories[k].push() on a duplicate and still cleared the draft, saved, and reopened the sheet — giving the user zero feedback that nothing happened when they typed an existing category name. Worse, if the user had picked a custom icon in catAddDraft.icon first, the DB.catIcon[catKey(k,v)]=catAddDraft.icon line still ran unconditionally, silently overwriting the icon of the pre-existing category with the same name. Fixed by adding the same early-return-with-toast guard used by addOwner/doRenameCat, which also fixes the icon-overwrite side effect since the function now returns before touching catIcon. Added addCat to the test harness's FUNCTIONS list and gave the sandbox toast() a lastToast recorder (previously a no-op) plus a catAddDraft field so it could be exercised; added 2 new regression tests (duplicate name toasts and leaves array/icon untouched; new name adds normally with no toast) — all 37 tests pass. Verified both inline <script> blocks still parse via new Function(). Bumped APP_VERSION 1.18.0→1.18.1 and sw.js CACHE v41→v42.
